text:
For a **pellet smoker**, I’d choose the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)** if you want a comfortable overnight margin or plan to charge campsite essentials too. It has **2,073.6 Wh** of capacity and a **2,600 W inverter**; the cited estimate is about **450–750 Wh for a 12-hour cook**, so it should leave reserve for cold weather or other devices. The source lists it at **$899**. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))

For a lighter-duty, **one-night option**, the **[BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)** has **1,152 Wh**—roughly enough for the estimated overnight cook, but with less cushion for lights, phones, or a particularly demanding setup. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))

Before buying, check your smoker’s label or manual for **startup/igniter wattage** and make sure the station’s inverter can handle it. Pellet grills draw a brief burst at ignition, then much less while cooking; the estimates above are for pellet grills, **not electric smokers with high-wattage heating elements**. ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill))
